items.title: 67255_Helen Humes oral history interview
items.q: I decided to travel with his band and I went with him... getting with the Basie Band... when we'd get down South we'd have to go over some ricketty bridges and Basie would say, 'stop the bus'.

ctx.x: Well anyway, that's where I was working when the Basie Band played in town. And after their gig, well they came, you know, to the Cotton Club and Basie heard me and he told me when he was talking to me, and he said, 'well I certainly enjoyed your singing'. He said, 'I'd like to have you come and sing with my band'. I said, 'yeah, who is your band?' He said, 'I'm sorry, I didn't introduce myself. I'm Count Basie'. I said, 'oh, well.' I said, 'well, how much do you pay?' He said, 'I pay $35 a week'. I said, 'Oh,…

him and ended up in New York. I started working for Androde at the Renaissance Ballroom. And so Mr. Androde asked Al if he could get me to come and sing on some special night it was. But they were having a big ball there and John Hammond was in the party. He came to this big reception and all this, and John Hammond was there and he heard me.
